commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Be'lakor, the Dark Master ({3}{U}{B}{R}, 6/5 flying legendary Demon Noble) has two abilities. Prince of Chaos: when Be'lakor enters, draw X cards and lose X life, where X is the number of Demons you control when the trigger resolves. Lord of Torment: whenever ANOTHER Demon you control enters, that entering Demon deals damage equal to ITS power to any target. The deck turns Demon power into damage. Cost reducers (Herald of Slaanesh, Urza's Incubator, Heartless Summoning, Ancient Cellarspawn) and cheat effects (Sneak Attack, Reanimate, Whip of Erebos, Gyruda, Patriarch's Bidding) put Demons in. Entry multipliers repeat the hits: Molten Echoes, Spark Double, Rite of Replication (kicked self-Rite: 25 Lord triggers, up to 150 damage, finite), Reflections of Littjara, Ghostly Flicker, Roaming Throne and Panharmonicon. Amplifiers raise the damage: Bloodletter of Aclazotz, Sower of Discord, Archfiend of Despair and Warstorm Surge. Liliana's Contract is an alternate win.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 (Optimized). Five Game Changers (Ancient Tomb, Cyclonic Rift, Demonic Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Vampiric Tutor). The only Spellbook combo is the finite Be'lakor + kicked Rite of Replication burst. Liliana's Contract is an alternate win. 36 lands. Not cEDH.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Each add raises Demon power per mana or protects the Demon board. Generic goodstuff Game Changers (Rhystic Study, Bolas's Citadel) were rejected, and so were Demons with self-defeating clauses (Abyssal Persecutor, Archfiend of the Dross). Demon count stays at 25 printed Demon cards plus Roaming Throne naming Demon.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: All 99 reviewed by quantity (94 rows, 100 physical; Island x3, Mountain x2, Swamp x4). The deck has 36 lands and 64 nonland cards, including 25 printed Demon cards (commander included) and 7 mana rocks plus Dark Ritual. Cost reduction: Herald of Slaanesh, Urza's Incubator, Heartless Summoning, Ancient Cellarspawn. Cheats: Sneak Attack, Reanimate, Whip, Gyruda, Patriarch's Bidding. Copy/blink: Molten Echoes, Spark Double, Rite, Reflections, Ghostly Flicker, Roaming Throne, Panharmonicon. Stack interaction: Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat. Removal: Chaos Warp, Deadly Rollick, Bedevil, Feed the Swarm, Cyclonic Rift, Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act, Rakdos the Showstopper. Two overlaps stand out. Blasphemous Act and Toxic Deluge are both symmetrical wipes, and Act kills our own board. Dream Devourer is a 0-power Demon whose Lord trigger deals 0.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Baseline: 36 lands + 7 rocks + Dark Ritual; average nonland MV 4.109. Curve by MV 1/2/3/4/5/6/7+: 4/13/10/12/9/9/7. Candidate: 36 lands + 6 rocks + Herald's Horn (Demon-only reduction) + Dark Ritual; average nonland MV 4.125. Curve: 4/11/11/13/9/9/7. Nonland pips U/B/R go from 15/58/20 to 15/65/17 (Reaper BBB, Belzenlok BB, Desecration BB, Dominance BB). Black land sources are unchanged: Swamp x4, Urborg, Underground Sea, Badlands, Blood Crypt, Watery Grave, Drowned Catacomb, Dragonskull Summit, Sunken Hollow, Foreboding Ruins, Luxury Suite, Xander's Lounge, Crumbling Necropolis, Morphic Pool, fetches, Command Tower, Path of Ancestry, Cavern of Souls (Demon), Exotic Orchard. Honest cost: one fewer generic rock for noncreature spells.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat. Removal: Chaos Warp, Deadly Rollick, Bedevil, Feed the Swarm, Cyclonic Rift, Toxic Deluge, Rakdos the Showstopper, plus Kindred Dominance (new, one-sided) and Reaper from the Abyss (new, repeatable). Graveyard hate stops Reanimate, Whip, Gyruda and Bidding. ETB hate (Torpor Orb, Hushbringer) stops Prince and Lord. Commander-removed state: Warstorm Surge, Kindred Discovery, Liliana's Contract, Unholy Annex and every Demon body still work.

material_candidates.role: Four-mana 6/6 flying Demon: the cheapest full-size Lord of Torment payload
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Dream Devourer's 0/3 body and its foretell discount (pay {2} on an earlier turn, then cast at MV-2). Cheap Demon count for Liliana's Contract and Prince X stays the same: one 2-3 MV Demon for one 4 MV Demon.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Be'lakor's Lord of Torment makes the ENTERING Demon deal damage equal to its power. Devourer enters as a 0-power Demon and deals 0. Desecration Demon deals 6 (12 to an opponent on our turn with Bloodletter) and costs {B}{B} after Herald of Slaanesh, or 2 with Urza's Incubator. Opponents who feed it a creature to tap it turn on Reaper from the Abyss's morbid and Harvester-style value.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: Opponents can tap it every combat by sacrificing a creature, so it is a poor attacker. Its value is the entry hit and the body, not combat.
material_candidates.reason: Best power-per-mana Demon in the pool. It turns a 0-damage trigger into a 6-damage one at the same curve slot. Archfiend of the Dross and Abyssal Persecutor are the same size but carry lose-the-game and can't-win clauses.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Be'lakor page (Sorceries, 5332/15693); live Scryfall Oracle
material_candidates.role: One-sided board wipe that names Demon
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Blasphemous Act's discount: Act often costs 1-4 mana on a full board, while Dominance is a flat 7. Ancient Cellarspawn (a Horror) still dies to our own Dominance.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Every creature we rely on is a Demon, and so are Roaming Throne naming Demon, Spark Double copying a Demon, and Plaguebearer tokens. Dominance keeps Be'lakor and the board; Act kills our own 6/5 and every Demon. The deck already has Toxic Deluge, Feed the Swarm and Rakdos, the Showstopper for cheap interaction.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: Seven mana at sorcery speed. Does nothing against Demon-tribal opponents, or against a noncreature threat.
material_candidates.reason: A deck that wins by keeping Demons on the battlefield should not run a symmetrical 13-damage wipe. Dominance is the one-sided version.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Be'lakor High Lift; live Scryfall Oracle
material_candidates.role: Six-mana 6/6 flying-trample Demon with immediate card advantage on entry
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Rakdos, Patron of Chaos's repeat end-step punisher: an opponent sacrifices two nonland nontoken permanents or we draw two. Red pips fall by one.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Same mana value, power and evasion, so the Lord of Torment hit is identical (6). Belzenlok's value is an ETB trigger, so Panharmonicon, Roaming Throne (naming Demon), Molten Echoes, Spark Double, Whip/Reanimate/Gyruda and Ghostly Flicker all repeat it. The deck's average nonland MV is 4.1, so the repeat clause fires often (about 2 cards, 2 damage to us).
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: Self-damage stacks with the Prince X life loss and Vilis. It is legendary, so a Molten Echoes copy dies to the legend rule after the trigger.
material_candidates.reason: Guaranteed, copyable, immediate cards beat a punisher where the opponent chooses, which needs an end step to survive and gives the choice away.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Be'lakor High Lift (4448/15693); live Scryfall Oracle
material_candidates.role: Six-mana 6/6 flying Demon with repeatable non-Demon removal at every end step
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Bloodthirster's extra-combat aggression (only if it connects, and it can't attack the same player twice). Red Demon count drops by one; Herald of Slaanesh still grants haste.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Same 6 power for the Lord of Torment hit. Morbid checks every end step (ours and opponents'). Be'lakor pings that kill creatures, Desecration Demon sacrifices, Kardur's goaded attackers, Toxic Deluge and chump blocks all enable it. The removal target is non-Demon, so it never hits our own board.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: BBB, and nothing happens unless a creature died that turn. Weak against Demon-tribal opponents.
material_candidates.reason: This deck is short on repeatable removal. Reaper turns Be'lakor's damage into a board-control engine, while Bloodthirster adds a second combat the deck rarely needs.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Five one-for-one swaps that raise Demon power per mana and protect the Demon board. (1) A 0-power Demon becomes a 6/6 for four. (2) A symmetrical wipe becomes a one-sided Demon wipe. (3) An opponent-choice punisher becomes immediate, copyable card advantage. (4) An extra-combat Demon becomes a repeatable non-Demon removal Demon. (5) A low-synergy rock becomes a Demon reducer that draws cards. Costs: Dominance is a flat 7 against Act's variable cost; red pips fall 20->17 while black rises 58->65; one fewer generic rock; no Bloodthirster extra combats; no foretell discount. Gains: total printed Demon power 129->135 with the same Demon count (25); a one-sided wipe; repeatable removal; more card flow.

low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Lord of Torment deals damage equal to the entering Demon's power, yet the list plays a 0-power Demon and a symmetrical wipe that kills its own Demons. Its two conditional 6-drops (Patron's punisher, Bloodthirster's extra combat) give value only after a turn cycle or a connected attack.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: After the five swaps, every remaining incumbent was re-read against the commander. Mana: 36 lands + 6 rocks + Horn is the floor; there was no further land or rock cut. Reduction and cheats (Herald, Incubator, Heartless, Cellarspawn, Sneak Attack, Reanimate, Whip, Gyruda, Bidding) are core. Copy/blink pieces (Echoes, Spark Double, Rite, Reflections, Flicker, Throne, Panharmonicon) are the payoff multipliers. Top end: Lord of Change, Archfiend of Despair, Valgavoth, Vilis and Rune-Scarred Demon are cheat targets with draw or finishing value. Kardur is the only defensive effect.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Courtyard fixes Demon spells for any color but is colorless for 30+ noncreature spells. Orchard usually taps for U/B/R. Staged as a six-swap alternative.
Same MV and power. Xander's discard/mill/sacrifice hits one opponent; Lord of Change draws three with flying and ward 3. Staged as a six-swap alternative.
Medallion removes the -1/-1 drawback (1 more damage per hit) but gives only -1 on black spells instead of -2 on every creature. A Horn-over-Heartless five-swap is also staged and rejected.
+1 power and upkeep draw for +1 MV; loses the only defensive or political effect.
Tutor engine vs the end-step doubling finisher; same top-end slot.
Pass C challenger: repeat blinks vs a commander-independent fallback. Kept Surge.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Courtyard always gives any color for the 25 Demon spells and Demon abilities, regardless of opponents' lands.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: It is colorless for every noncreature spell (Mana Drain, Rite, Sneak Attack, Dominance). Orchard taps for Grixis colors in most pods.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Xander's three modes punish one opponent hard and are copyable by Echoes and Spark Double.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Lord of Change's draw three refuels after Prince life payments, and ward 3 protects it. Xander has no evasion.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Seven-swap: maximum Demon-specific fixing (Courtyard) plus Xander's copyable hand, library and permanent disruption.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: It combines both rejected trades (Orchard's noncreature colors and Lord of Change's draw-three plus ward), and neither beat its incumbent alone, so stacking them would be padding.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: Stopped at five. The remaining weak-looking slots (Orchard, Lord of Change, Heartless Summoning, Kardur, Archfiend of Despair, Abyssal Harvester, Crumbling Necropolis, Warstorm Surge) each have a concrete role a challenger loses: noncreature-spell colors, draw plus ward, -2 ramp, the only defensive effect, the finisher, a cheap Demon copier, tri-color fixing, or the commander-independent fallback. No sixth trade was a clear upgrade on quality.
